chunk_findings.detail: The `clean_merge_conclusion` exemption is placed *after* the scope test, so it can never fire in the default configuration, contradicting the contract the new knob advertises. With the default `[enforce].merge_commit_scope = "own"`, `_commit_scope` returns at the first branch (`return _merge_own_paths(tree, paths)`) and never reaches `if lease and paths and clean_merge_conclusion(tree): return []`; the exemption only exists under `"all"`. Concrete input: branch and `main` both edit `src/a.py` in non-overlapping regions; `git merge main` produces a clean, non-conflicted result, so `clean_merge_conclusion(tree)` is true and the commit is "exactly git's automatic merge". `src/a.py` is still in the staged set (the merge result differs from `HEAD`) and is part of the paths `_merge_own_paths`/the "own" filter keeps, so the lease check is applied to it and can refuse the merge. Running the same command with `merge_commit_scope = "all"` returns `[]` and allows it. That is the opposite of both claims made by the change: the knob doc says "A merge that is exactly git's automatic merge is exempt from the lease check either way", and `strictest=("all", "every path the merge stages is judged")` asserts `"all"` is the strictest value, yet for an automatic merge it is strictly *weaker* than the default (it judges nothing on the lease check while `"own"` judges the same-file paths). The exemption (or the scope dispatch) needs to be ordered so the automatic-merge case is handled before the scope branch, since as written the guard is dead code for the default value.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/enforce.py:1239 (`_commit_scope`)

chunk_findings.detail: `staged_diff` documents and types `paths` as the filter that "limits it to those files"; `None` means "no filter". But `paths=[]` is a distinct, valid input (it is exactly the value a caller can produce after intersecting staged paths with a branch-changed set that turned out empty), and it is not handled: the code still emits the pathspec separator, so the command becomes `git diff --cached ... --`. Git treats a bare `--` as "everything after this is a path" with nothing after it, i.e. no pathspec at all, so `staged_diff(repo, [])` returns the **full** staged diff rather than the empty string. That silently reintroduces the exact failure the change is fixing: a caller that filtered down to zero files (e.g. a merge whose staged content is entirely the merged parent's) would get every staged path judged instead of none. The one call site in `enforce.py` happens to be protected by the preceding `if not own: return Verdict(OK, "")` guard, so the bug is latent today, but the new parameter's contract is violated for `paths=[]`; the guard should be `if paths:` (falling back to `None`) or the caller must never pass an empty list. Reported because `paths: list[str] | None` explicitly admits `[]` and any future/other caller (e.g. a scope that legitimately resolves to zero paths) will get the whole diff back.

chunk_findings.detail:
`docsync.staged_diff` is a shared helper — its own docstring covers the commit-hook's merge case, while the module is the docs-refresh pipeline. Before this change an empty `paths` list produced no `--` pathspec, so git answered with the whole staged diff: an empty selection meant "unfiltered". The change redefines `[]` as "select nothing" and returns `""`.

That is what the merge hook wants, but the same helper is the natural place for the docs-side filter, which is fed the `[export].documents` selection — documented in this very diff as "`documents` (the selection, default `[]`)". With the default configuration, a caller that passes that selection straight through now gets `""` instead of the full staged diff, so `ddflow` computes "no staged doc changes" and refreshes/exports nothing, whereas before it saw every changed document. The added test only pins the hook's usage (`staged_diff(merging, []) == ""`); it does not cover the docs caller, whose empty default is exactly the value whose meaning just inverted. Either the empty selection must keep meaning "unfiltered" (and the hook must pass `None`/a computed non-empty list) or every `[]`-as-all caller must be converted to `None` in the same change.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docsync.py:233 (`staged_diff` empty-filter early return)

chunk_findings.detail: The change adds the knob row `| \`enforce.merge_commit_scope\` | \`"own"\` | \`own\` \| \`all\` |` and bumps every count from 263 to 264, but no code in this change (part 1 of 1) defines or reads `enforce.merge_commit_scope`; the string appears only in README. The README itself states the table is generated and "a test fails when it differs, so its count and defaults cannot drift", so a hand-added row over a 263-knob schema makes the generated `README/knobs` block (now sha `d1345f2e6260`) differ from what the generator renders and the latch test fails. If instead the key is tolerated without a schema entry, then `enforce.merge_commit_scope = "all"` is silently ignored — a documented knob that has no reader — and nothing in the diff implements the selection it advertises. Either way the artifact is inconsistent with its own claim: `ddflow config --set enforce.merge_commit_scope all` cannot change merge-scope checking because no enforcement code consumes the key.
chunk_findings.title: README.md:5871 (`enforce.merge_commit_scope`)

chunk_findings.detail: `test_an_automatic_merge_of_a_file_both_sides_changed_passes_by_default` cannot detect the regression it is meant to pin. `shared.txt` is unleased, so in the staged merge `git diff --cached` reports a clean auto-merge of a file with no lease and the commit succeeds regardless of whether the hook checks the merged-parent change. The reported failure ("merging main into a branch was refused by the lease check for files that came from main") requires a *leased* file that only changed on main; using an unleased file means this test passes identically before and after the change, so the fix could regress to checking merged-parent files again and the suite would stay green (indeed the unchanged test ending at line 156 still asserts the merge is refused because of a file from main, which is the behavior the intent says must go away — the two tests cannot both describe the intended semantics).
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_hook_merge_scope.py:169
